dedupe_keys.name: venezuela june 2026 earthquake sentinel 1 likelihood of damaged structures conflict ecology

description: Conflict Ecology produced a rapid assessment of building damage from the 24 June 2026 Venezuela earthquake, an M7.5 mainshock after an M7.2 foreshock near San Felipe and Yumare, using Sentinel-1 radar coherent change detection. Version 1, published on HDX on 11 July 2026, covers the whole area of Copernicus EMS activation EMSR884 and all ground with modified Mercalli intensity VI or more, monitoring 2,699,969 Overture Maps building footprints, and estimates that 69,431 buildings were likely damaged or destroyed as of the satellite pass of 1 July 2026. Each footprint carries a confidence tier (possible, probable or high confidence) describing how anomalous the post-event signal is, not how severe the damage is; district-level damage shares and Spanish and English slide decks are included. Coverage: north-central Venezuela including the central coast and greater Caracas. Access: GeoJSON and GeoPackage files on HDX. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: this is an indicator of surface change consistent with damage, not confirmation for any building, and detected damage can range from light to collapse; against undamaged controls the false-alarm rate is about 3% at the possible tier and under 1% at high confidence. Simulation uses are prioritising inspections and comparing observed damage patterns with shaking-based loss estimates. Related records: the IMPACT Sentinel-1 damage proxy and the DISHA analysis for the same event.
